pr752.body:
This PR verifies the `smallsort` module (#56) with Kani on the real implementations, within explicit bounds: memory safety of the three `small_sort` trait entries and the helpers behind them at lengths that reach every dispatch boundary up to N32; sorting correctness (sortedness plus full-value multiset preservation) on the general, fallback and network routes; and `requires`/`modifies` contracts on five real helpers, proved and then used at real call sites. 235 harnesses run `SUCCESSFUL` on each OS in the repository's unchanged Kani workflow, and 13 negative controls check that the oracles and contracts reject what they should. Function bodies, signatures, workflows and tool pins are unchanged. **Highlights** - **Memory safety on the real routes.** All three trait entries (stable, unstable, unstable-Freeze) and the general, fallback and network routes behind them run as-is, at representative lengths that include every dispatch boundary up to N32. Comparators return arbitrary answers or mutate through a `Cell`; element types include a Drop type, a ZST and sizes of 1, 8, 16, 17, 85 and 86 bytes, which select every size-dependent branch. - **Sorting correctness with a full-value oracle.** Sortedness plus multiset preservation, stated for an arbitrary symbolic value: it occurs as often after the sort as before. Some families sort by a key (`x >> 1`) under which distinct values tie, so a key-only oracle would miss payload corruption; the network and logical-model families use the ordinary `<`. Covered on the general and stable routes at u8 and u64 N0..9, on the fallback route at N0..6, and on the network route (sortedness up to N13, multiset preservation below the network width, and permutation of distinct tags at N9 and N13 for an arbitrary comparator). - **Contracts on the real helpers.** `requires`/`modifies` on `swap_if_less`, `insert_tail`, `insertion_sort_shift_left`, `sort4_stable` and `bidirectional_merge`, proved by 16 `proof_for_contract` harnesses with an arbitrary-answer comparator, and used by four `stub_verified` consumers at real call sites with the same element type, comparator and allocation as the proof (the u8 networks at N9, N13 and N32; u64 `sort8_stable`). - **Sorting contracts where this Kani accepts them.** `ensures` (model-sorted output, preserved full-value count) on proof-owned profiles of the helpers and on wrappers of the three trait entries at N2. Contracts directly on the trait methods are blocked by two Kani issues we reported with reproducers (Limitations). - **Calibrated negative controls.** Thirteen harnesses: a mutant `swap_if_less`, payload corruptions, wrong comparators, `requires` violations, a comparator writing outside the write set, a duplicated tag. Each fails exactly its designated check on this library tree with the pinned Kani. ## Challenge criteria | Criterion | In this PR | |---|---| | No UB: the three `small_sort` trait entries | real routes at representative lengths up to N32 on the type matrix below, Kani default checks | | No UB: `swap_if_less`, `insertion_sort_shift_left`, `sort4_stable`, `has_efficient_in_place_swap` | contracts proved on the listed domains (first three); real bodies with arbitrary comparators; `insertion_sort_shift_left` body at every offset for u64 N1..20; predicate on 12 types | | Contracts showing that `small_sort` sorts | `ensures` on N2 wrappers of each entry; sorting proved by harness oracles at the lengths below; contracts on the trait methods themselves await [kani#5116](https://github.com/model-checking/kani/issues/5116) and [kani#4908](https://github.com/model-checking/kani/issues/4908#issuecomment-6606217149) | | Lengths | bounded as listed; correctness to N9 (general, stable), N13 (network sortedness), N6 (fallback) | | UB classes | dangling, misaligned and out-of-bounds accesses on every path above; see Limitations for the rest |
What is checked (235 harnesses, organizer flags including --no-assert-contracts) | Group | Harnesses | Route / function | T, N | Property | |---|---:|---|---|---| | General / stable entries | 25 | general route (`small_sort_general*`) | u8, u64; N0..9 | key order + full-value count | | Fallback insertion | 7 | `small_sort_fallback` | u8, u64; N0..6 | key order + full-value count | | Network entry | 16 | `small_sort_network` | u8 N0..7, 9..13; u64 N0..7, 9 | order; count only for N < 9 | | Insertion phase | 5 | `insertion_sort_shift_left` from offset 9 or 13 | u8 N10, 11, 14; u64 N10, 14 | whole-array count, any input | | Safety | 92 | all routes and dispatch | u64, u8, `[u8; 16/17/85/86]`, a Drop type, ZST (stable trait entry, `()`), `Cell`; dispatch to N32; insertion at every offset for u64 N1..20 and `Cell` N1..5, N20; stable route with minimal scratch at N2 | Kani default checks up to normal return | | Drop / tag | 19 | fallback, insertion, general and network routes | selected N; fixed distinct u8 tags on network N9, N13 | drop counts and tag permutation at normal return | | Trait entries, logical model | 6 | `small_sort` | `Cell`, Drop key | logical order + count | | Helpers | 9 | `has_efficient_in_place_swap`, `sort4_stable`, `swap_if_less` at equal positions, helper pairs | type matrix; N2, N4, N10 | predicate; safety + value preservation | | Contract proofs on profiles | 36 | `swap_if_less` 14, `sort4_stable` 2, `insert_tail` 5, `bidirectional_merge` 12, N2 forwarding wrappers 3 | exact listed allocations | order contract on the executed domain | | Contracts on the real helpers | 20 | `proof_for_contract` 16, `stub_verified` consumers 4 | see Contracts | `requires` and `modifies` on the executed domain | Full-value multiset preservation uses an independent symbolic probe on the listed integer and byte-array fixtures; `Cell` and Drop fixtures use their logical models. The tag harnesses sort fixed distinct u8 tags with an arbitrary comparator; that this carries over to arbitrary values (data moves only by comparator answers) is a source-level argument.
## Contracts **On the real helpers.** Safety contracts: `requires` on pointer validity and allocation geometry, `modifies` on the element or destination memory. Executed domains: - `swap_if_less`: u8, u64 and `[u8; 17]` in a 4-element allocation; u8 in 9- and 13-element allocations; u8 and u64 in a 32-element allocation with any base and any two positions, equal positions included. - `insert_tail`: u64, tail 1..4 in a 5-element allocation, and tail 1..15 from the start of a 17-element allocation. - `insertion_sort_shift_left`: u64 arrays of lengths 2 and 3, every valid offset. The body itself is also checked directly at every offset for lengths 1 through 20. - `sort4_stable`: u64, disjoint 4-element source and destination. - `bidirectional_merge`: u64 of length 2 and 4, and of length 8 at the geometry of the 48-element stable scratch. Each consumer replaces the real call with the proved contract through `stub_verified`, with the same element type, comparator and allocation domain as the contract proof: the unstable u8 network at N9, N13 and N32 with `swap_if_less`, and u64 `sort8_stable` with `bidirectional_merge`. The same routes are also checked with their real bodies. Proofs on the real helpers use one comparator function item per harness that returns an arbitrary answer, so no ordering law is assumed. Only the executed domains are claimed. **On profiles.** Sorting contracts (`ensures`: model-sorted output, preserved full-value count) are checked on proof-owned profiles that forward a fixed element type and one canonical function-pointer comparator to the real helpers (a guard rejects any other comparator), and on three N2 wrappers that call the trait entry points.
Negative controls (13, behind cfg(kani_smallsort_controls), which CI never sets) - a negated `swap_if_less` copy; - two checks that the oracle sees a changed payload; - the canonical-comparator guard of the wrappers; - four consumers that use a profile contract with a wrong comparator, so the comparator precondition must fail; - three calls that violate a real helper's `requires`: out-of-allocation `swap_if_less`, `insert_tail` with `begin == tail`, and `bidirectional_merge` into an overlapping destination; - a `swap_if_less` contract proof with a comparator that increments a captured counter, which must fail the write-set check; - a duplicated tag on the network N9 tag harness. We ran all thirteen on this library tree with the pinned Kani (`cd355b0b`), outside GitHub Actions: each fails exactly one check, the designated one ([report](https://github.com/Tiramisu-Cake/verify-rust-std/blob/fc72b711781e2c0effb3fc1d33dfad55785bd5b2/research/challenge-8/kani-k1/en/negative-controls.md)).
## CI We ran the upstream workflows unchanged on this commit in our fork via `workflow_dispatch` (fork runs, not upstream PR checks): - Kani [run 42363378063](https://github.com/Tiramisu-Cake/verify-rust-std/actions/runs/42363378063): `success` on Ubuntu and macOS, including all 8 partition jobs, autoharness and `Build JSON from logs`, in attempt 1. - Rust Tests, Flux, RAPx, KMIR, VeriFast, VeriFast (negative), GOTO Transcoder, Book and Testable SIMD: `success` in attempt 1. In the autoharness runs all 235 SmallSort harnesses are `SUCCESSFUL` on each OS, with zero failed checks and 978/978 satisfied covers (counted from the logs; the workflow does not enforce covers). No warning comes from the SmallSort files. SmallSort's summed verification time is 7,802 s on Ubuntu and 10,534 s on macOS, 65.9% and 70.3% of the job's manual-harness total; the longest proof takes 246 s on Ubuntu and 340 s on macOS, below the 600 s timeout ([per-harness timings](https://github.com/Tiramisu-Cake/verify-rust-std/blob/e63e7fadfdc8a9e4871f872fdf022092cbb7387e/research/challenge-8/kani-k1/v10cci/README.md)). The harnesses are independent: any of them can be split or moved behind the opt-in cfg without touching the rest. At this base the autoharness job runs on a pull request only with the `run-autoharness` label (or in the merge queue or on dispatch); we would appreciate the label on this PR. ## Limitations Several of the remaining gaps come from Kani limitations that we reported or reproduced upstream; they are linked below. - **Scope.** Results hold for the listed types, comparators, lengths and allocation layouts. The write sets list element and destination memory only, since Kani cannot state the footprint of an arbitrary `FnMut`; the contracts are claimed for comparators that write nowhere else (a comment above `swap_if_less` says so, and the counter control checks it). - **Contracts on the trait methods.** A contract on a specialization `default fn` is not accepted on the current pin ([kani#5116](https://github.com/model-checking/kani/issues/5116)), nor is a `proof_for_contract` on a trait method with its own generic `F` ([kani#4908](https://github.com/model-checking/kani/issues/4908#issuecomment-6606217149)); the N2 wrappers are the nearest contract-form statement this Kani verifies. Kani main has since fixed the second case ([kani#5135](https://github.com/model-checking/kani/pull/5135)), which is not yet in the repository's pin; it opens direct contracts on the non-default `small_sort` implementations, which we intend to add here once the pin includes it. - **Lengths.** Wider domains are limited by verification time; an extended u64 N10 composition on an earlier research tree also ran into `kani-driver` memory use ([kani#5117](https://github.com/model-checking/kani/issues/5117)). - **Panics.** Seventy-one ordinary harnesses replace `panic_on_ord_violation` with an `assume(false)` stub; the other 164 do not replace that function. Comparator panics and unwind recovery are not verified. - **UB classes.** As in the repository's Kani profile, there is no uninitialized-memory or value-validity instrumentation on these routes: `-Z uninit-checks` reports unsupported operations here ([kani#3300](https://github.com/model-checking/kani/issues/3300)) and `-Z valid-value-checks` does not yet support `copy_nonoverlapping` ([kani#3762](https://github.com/model-checking/kani/issues/3762)), which these routes use. Writes to immutable bytes and aliasing beyond Kani's pointer checks are not modelled. - **Model trust.** The array-select reproducer from [kani#5104](https://github.com/model-checking/kani/issues/5104) still fails on the organizer Kani pin `cd355b0b` ([pin-check report](https://github.com/Tiramisu-Cake/verify-rust-std/blob/fc72b711781e2c0effb3fc1d33dfad55785bd5b2/research/challenge-8/kani-k1/en/kani-pin-check.md)); the four array-valued fixtures `network::swap_contract_bytes16_n2`, `network::swap_contract_bytes17_n2`, `merge::sort4_contract_bytes16_n4` and `merge::sort4_arbitrary_comparator_bytes16_n4` retain that model caveat. - **ZST and geometry.** ZST coverage consists of direct stable SmallSort trait-entry checks on `()`. The public sort entry points short-circuit ZSTs, and `select_nth_unstable` skips selection work for them after validating the index. ZST comparators read with `ptr::read`, since `read_volatile` on a ZST gives spurious dereference failures ([kani#5072](https://github.com/model-checking/kani/issues/5072)). The stable Freeze route is checked with a separate 48-element scratch and with the minimal scratch at N2. Tie stability is not proved separately. Beyond this PR: wider domains (longer networks, more insertion lengths) need more verification time or tool support; we left them out rather than stretch the CI budget, and can propose them separately. **Note for maintainers.** The `sort4_stable` contract makes source/destination non-overlap explicit. The existing SAFETY comment mentions validity for four reads and writes but does not state this condition; the implementation uses `copy_nonoverlapping`. **Source.** One [commit](https://github.com/Tiramisu-Cake/verify-rust-std/commit/872d5a43380752786415bc00d2a12ce0e930cb37) on `main` at `233f96f66a` (it merges cleanly with the current `main`): 17 files under `library/`, +3941/−0. The harnesses live in `core::slice::sort::shared::smallsort::verify` (`verify.rs` opens with a module map). `smallsort.rs` gains only the contract attributes, a comment on their write sets, three `cfg(kani)` geometry predicates used by the contracts and the `mod verify` registration; `library/core/Cargo.toml` gets a `check-cfg` entry for the controls cfg. This contribution was prepared with the help of AI assistants. By submitting this pull request, I confirm that my contribution is made under the terms of the Apache 2.0 and MIT licenses.
